items.title: The zero scheme of a regular section of an ample invertible sheaf on a connected proper scheme of depth at least two is connected
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the zero scheme of a regular section s of an ample invertible sheaf on a connected proper scheme whose local rings have depth at least two is connected. The proof argues by contradiction: the vanishing schemes Z(s^n) have the same underlying topological space as Z(s), so a disconnected Z(s) would give a nontrivial idempotent in R_n = Gamma(X, O_{Z(s^n)}), hence the map Gamma(X, O_X) -> R_n is not an isomorphism; reading that off the canonical short exact sequence 0 -> L^{-n} -> O_X -> O_{Z(s^n)} -> 0 forces either H^0(X, L^{-n}) or H^1(X, L^{-n}) to be nonzero for infinitely many n, contradicting the two vanishing theorems for negative twists (proof lines 11308-11328). H3: the idempotent-to-cohomology transfer and the use of both vanishing theorems in one contradiction are independent research-level moves.
